findings.title: Several SQL-phase producers have no admitted 600-second hard bound
findings.problem: Evidence classification: direct inspection of the executed driver, not an observed timeout. The admitted contract is hard producer 600 seconds plus driver 2400 seconds. run() invokes commands directly; only sql_run explicitly supplies timeout -k 15 600. Readiness, database readback, docker rm, receipt/ownership helpers and the direct docker run are not producer-bounded. setup_sql.inspect bounds its own inspection to 30 seconds, but that does not bound sqlprobe's whole readiness/readback or docker rm. In particular, a blocked readback query can consume the remaining outer deadline before cleanup reaches docker rm; the outer driver's eventual kill grace is not a substitute for returning control after the producer deadline and independently attempting cleanup. Preparation/check producers are likewise mostly unwrapped. The recorded SQL phase finished in about 75 seconds with successful readback/removal, so no overrun or leaked container is demonstrated by this run; nevertheless the blanket hard-producer claim is false.
findings.suggested_fix: Do not change or rerun anything under this report. If Root separately grants any future driver work, apply the admitted producer timeout centrally (including readiness/readback and Docker operations), record timeout/kill exits as INVALID, and leave bounded independent cleanup opportunity within the outer deadline. Preserve these actual scripts/logs. Until explicitly dispositioned, describe this execution as having bounded test producers and an outer driver bound, not universal producer-bound conformity.

findings.title: Cleanup can report success despite failed unlink or failed absence verification
findings.problem: Evidence classification: concrete failure-path defect in the executed driver; not an observed cleanup failure. run() always returns zero and communicates producer status only in LAST_RC. After unlink-private, cleanup ignores LAST_RC, prints crc=0 and can let the overall driver exit zero even if unlink raised. For absence verification, every nonzero docker inspect is accepted, not specifically 'no such object', and docker ps is piped into wc without pipefail: a daemon/query error can become a successful count of zero. Unlink also runs even after owned-check/removal/absence failure, contrary to the grant to unlink those exact credential/SQLGuard files after container removal. Thus the fail-closed cleanup contract is not met on these paths. Actual logs 85-89 show successful removal, the specific no-such-object diagnostic, empty matching count, scan zero and all four files unlinked with exit zero, so the recorded run has positive independent cleanup evidence despite this driver defect.
findings.suggested_fix: No automatic repair/rerun authority. For any separately authorized future driver, preserve the original primary while aggregating every cleanup producer status, distinguish actual not-found from failed inspection, preserve the Docker query exit separately from counting output, and unlink only after positive owned-removal/absence confirmation. Check unlink's exit and exact expected removals; retain private files when removal is unresolved. Preserve the current artifacts and route the unmet error-path contract to Root rather than labeling all cleanup paths proven.
